    <Axiom id="AX_SCOPE_TABLE_FORMAT">
      Scopes table in the Portal: each row = link to the scope spec + scope-type + status emoji + one-line description.
      - ✅ — spec exists and is approved.
      - 🚧 — spec being authored / `discovery` not yet run.
      - Status is derived purely from the presence of `specs/<scope>/<scope>.spec.md`.
    </Axiom>

    <Axiom id="AX_VISION_ONLY_FOR_APPLICATION">
      The `## Vision` section in the Portal is present only when the project contains at least one product or library scope. For tooling-only repos (sandboxes, infra repos) the Vision section is omitted.
    </Axiom>

    <Axiom id="AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED">
      Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line,
      the expanded part in parentheses: `<ACR>-DL-N <date> — <decision> (почему: …; отвергнуто: …;
      риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already
      recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify
      and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
    </Axiom>

    <Axiom id="AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK">
      A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/<scope>`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.
    </Axiom>

  <ChatProtocol>
    <Contract id="QUESTION_FORMAT">
      Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A
      `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words, without numbering and
      without semantic question IDs; under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool
      call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by
      `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do
      not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the
      recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the
      explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short
      labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.

      Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually
      independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets
      of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview
      sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.

      Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain
      text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator
      can answer by name; skipping the explanation and firing a bare list of options is itself the
      violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).

      Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`
      (not the first typical answer):

      Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:

      ### 💡 Куда положить ресёрч-документ
      Документ можно держать рядом со спекой — виден в контексте скоупа, проще найти, пока читаешь
      её — или в общем каталоге ресёрчей, если он пригодится за пределами одного скоупа; для разового
      ресёрча под конкретную спеку разница небольшая.
      ✅ **Рядом со спекой** `[specs/<scope>/research/]` — виден в контексте скоупа, не потеряется.
      Иначе:
        Once the operator answers, the agent does NOT compress the answer — it NORMALIZES it while
        ROUTING every semantic anchor to the artifact it actually belongs to; dropping an anchor is a
        loss, but filing it under the wrong artifact is a second, independent loss (a release boundary
        misread as the target state, or a target state watered down by a caveat that only applies to v1).
        Three anchor kinds, three homes:
        - **Target state** — what the finished thing does, for whom, the full shape of the outcome →
          Vision, worded as the COMPLETE goal with no release caveat folded in. «Синхронизация между
          устройствами» stays the target even when v1 ships without it.
        - **Deferred / release-boundary decision** — «в v1 без бэкенда», «пока без синхронизации», «не
          сейчас» → a `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`, marked deferred.
          Example: operator says «v1 строго local-only, без бэкенда» while the goal is full sync → Vision
          keeps «полная синхронизация между устройствами» as the target, and the Decision Log gets

          синхронизации; риск: придётся менять модель хранения данных)`.
        - **Technical/stack preference** — a named framework, «готовый UIKit», a design-system pick →

    <Axiom id="AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE" cross-cutting="true">
      Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my
      read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list,
      derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the
      questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need
      the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.
    </Axiom>

    <!-- portal-structure / infra-base-minimal-spec formats load lazily at their write step — see ExecutionPlan. -->
    <Contract id="DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT">
      One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries
      only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.

      ```markdown
      <ACR>-DL-N <date> — <decision in one phrase> (почему: <compromise/criterion>; отвергнуто: <alternative — why not>; риск: <if accepted>)
      ```

      An autonomous-execute deviation appends one final typed token to that SAME line:
      `[verdict: pending-operator]`. The only replacements are `[verdict: accepted]`,
      `[verdict: rework]`, and `[verdict: rolled-back]`; only `pending-operator` is open.

      **ID.** `<ACR>-DL-<N>` — spec acronym first, exactly like a Task-ID and like `<ACR>-REQ-<N>`
      (`REQUIREMENT_ENTRY_FORMAT`); `<N>` is sequential within THIS spec only — the acronym gives global
      uniqueness, not the number. This is the only grammar for NEW entries. Existing append-only
      file-local `D-N` entries remain immutable and resolvable as legacy references; never create another;
      conflicts (a duplicate number inside one spec) are caught mechanically, the same way as for
      `<ACR>-REQ-<N>`.

      Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: <ACR>-DL-M` to the parenthetical instead of a
      separate field — the entry stays one line. `<date>` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status
      (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose
